intro: A product manager who shows outcomes, not activity: launches with adoption and revenue numbers, and evidence of working through other people.
tips: Write outcomes (adoption, revenue, retention), not ceremonies (ran standups).
Show how you decided: research, data, experiments.
Make your scope clear: team size, product, customers.

basics.name: Daniel Kim
basics.label: Senior Product Manager
basics.summary: Product manager with seven years in B2B SaaS. Took a scheduling product from 0 to 4,000 paying teams, and led the pricing change that grew average revenue per account by 22%.

work.name: Shiftly
work.summary: Workforce scheduling for hospitality, 4,000 paying teams.
highlights: Launched the mobile app that 70% of shift workers now use weekly.
Led a pricing and packaging change, informed by 40 customer interviews, that grew revenue per account by 22%.
Worked with a team of 8 engineers and 2 designers; introduced quarterly outcome goals the company adopted.

work.name: Brightdesk
work.summary: Help desk software for mid-sized companies.
highlights: Shipped the knowledge base that deflected 18% of support tickets for customers who used it.
Ran 25 A/B tests on onboarding; activation rose from 31% to 46%.
